This unauthorized enrollment has led to significant overdraft fees being deducted from my account, which I did not agree to or request.

When I contacted Wells Fargo for clarification, I was informed that I was enrolled in this " protection '' service, which is supposed to prevent overdrafts and associated fees. However, I was never notified of this automatic enrollment, nor did I ever give my consent to be included in this program. I believe that this practice is a deliberate tactic by Wells Fargo to siphon money from unsuspecting customers.

Wells Fargo has a documented history of unethical overdraft practices, including a recent {$3.00} XXXX settlement with the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) in XX/XX/year> over similar allegations of improper practices. I would like to address my rights under 15 U.S. Code 1635, which pertains to the right of rescission under the Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ). 

This law provides borrowers the right to rescind certain loan agreements within three business days from the date of the transaction or the date of receiving required disclosures, whichever is later. Additionally, in cases where the necessary disclosures were not provided, the right to rescind may be extended up to three years from the transaction date.

To ensure compliance, I kindly request the following : 1. Full Disclosure Documents : A copy of the original loan agreement and all disclosures provided at the time of the loans initiation. 
2. Itemized Accounting : A detailed breakdown of the charges, interest, and payments associated with the loan.

3. Verification of Charge-Off : Documentation substantiating the charge-off, including the date and amount.

If disclosures were not properly provided as required by TILA, I may have grounds to rescind the loan agreement. Please review my account and provide clarification on this matter within the timeframe mandated by applicable laws. 

I look forward to your prompt response to resolve this issue amicably. Please direct all correspondence to the address listed above or contact me at XXXX.

complaints.sub_issue: Didn't receive notice of right to dispute
complaints.consumer_complaint_narrative:
I am submitting this complaint against Midland Credit Management XXXX XXXX regarding their handling of a debt collection lawsuit filed against me, case number XXXX XXXX, in the Special Civil Part, XXXX XXXX XXXX New Jersey XXXX The case, initiated on XX/XX/XXXX, resulted in a default judgment entered by the clerk on XX/XX/XXXX, with an initial demand amount of {$950.00}. I believe Midland Credit Management has engaged in unfair and potentially predatory debt collection practices, and I am requesting the CFPB to investigate their actions. 

Despite my efforts to address this matter, I was unable to properly respond to the lawsuit due to inadequate notice and unclear communication regarding critical case deadlines. Throughout the proceedings, I submitted multiple letters and objections to the court, including correspondence on XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX, and XX/XX/XXXX. I also filed objections to the wage garnishment initiated by Midland Credit Management. However, the plaintiff proceeded to request a writ of execution against my wages, which was issued on XX/XX/XXXX. I believe the wage garnishment process was unfairly pursued without consideration of my financial circumstances or a meaningful effort to resolve the matter outside of court. 

I also filed a Motion to Vacate Default XXXX on XX/XX/XXXX, which is currently pending and scheduled for a decision on XX/XX/XXXX. This motion highlights the procedural deficiencies that led to the default judgment, including insufficient notification of the plaintiffs motions and my inability to adequately defend myself. Furthermore, I requested an adjournment of the wage execution hearing originally scheduled for XX/XX/XXXX, which was later rescheduled for XX/XX/XXXX. 

I am concerned that Midland Credit Managements actions, along with the conduct of their legal counsel, violated principles of fairness and may have breached the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ). Their failure to provide timely notice and adequate communication deprived me of the opportunity to respond effectively and defend my case. Additionally, their pursuit of wage garnishment without addressing my objections or financial situation raises questions about their compliance with federal regulations governing debt collection practices.

Additionally, had Midland made offers in the form of a payoff presentment, following due process accordingly in good faith, I would have made the necessary arrangements to enter into good faith negotiations to suffice the debt. Instead, it appears that Midland feels that they do not have to follow the law in its entirety and pick and choose what best serves their bottom line. Since they have basically flaunted the law, I am seeking remedy and relief as well as disciplinary actions against Midland Credit Management , Inc for their blatant disregard for due process of law.

complaints.consumer_complaint_narrative:
I am writing to file a formal complaint against State Employees Credit Union ( SECU ) concerning their improper handling of negotiable instruments I provided and the subsequent inaccurate reporting to credit agencies. 

As an informed consumer, I understand the obligations financial institutions have under the Uniform Commercial Code ( UCC ), particularly regarding the processing of negotiable instruments. According to UCC 3-104, a negotiable instrument is defined as an unconditional promise or order to pay a fixed amount of money, payable to bearer or to order at the time it is issued or first comes into possession of a holder, and payable on demand or at a definite time. 

In accordance with these provisions, I submitted certified negotiable instruments to SECU as payments. However, SECU failed to process these instruments appropriately. Some were ignored without justification, and others were neither processed nor returned to me. This negligence has led to unauthorized transfers of my securities to third-party agencies without my consent.

Furthermore, SECU closed my account without proper notice and reported inaccurate information to credit reporting agencies, adversely affecting my credit standing.

I request the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau to investigate SECUs actions concerning : 1. The mishandling and non-return of negotiable instruments I provided.

2. Unauthorized transfer of my securities to third parties.

3. The closure of my account without due process.

4. The dissemination of false information to credit reporting agencies.

I seek remediation for the financial and reputational harm caused by SECUs actions and assurance that such practices are rectified to prevent future occurrences. 

Thank you for your attention to this matter.

complaints.consumer_complaint_narrative:
I have been a loyal Wells Fargo customer for over 25 years, beginning with a personal banking account while in law school and later entrusting the bank with my business accounts. Given this longstanding relationship, I expected a higher standard of service and accountability, especially when dealing with unauthorized transactions and disputed charges. Unfortunately, my recent experience has been deeply frustrating and financially damaging. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, I contacted Wells Fargo to request stop payment orders on disputed charges from five merchants : XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX These requests were for two separate business accounts, and I clearly explained to the agenton a recorded linethat the charges were unauthorized, that I had already communicated with the merchants regarding the disputes, and that I needed the bank to stop any further withdrawals. The claim numbers assigned to these requests were : XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX While three of the stop payment orders were processed successfully, two were not. Despite my explicit request, these merchants continued withdrawing funds from my accounts. When I realized this, I called Wells Fargo again. Unfortunately, the agent I spoke with was unprofessional and seemed distractedhe repeatedly called me " XXXX '' ( which is not my name ) and referenced transactions from XX/XX/XXXX, which had nothing to do with my case. Without explanation, he abruptly transferred me to another agent, forcing me to start the process over again after already spending over 30 minutes on the phone. 

The next agent showed no concern for the inconvenience I had already endured. Nevertheless, I proceeded to re-file stop orders for the two remaining merchants and requested a refund for the unauthorized withdrawals, resulting in two new claim numbers : XXXX XXXX At this point, I had zero confidence that my requests would be handled correctly. To ensure action was taken, I went into my local Wells Fargo branch and met with a business banker. She was the only Wells Fargo representative who demonstrated professionalism and a willingness to help. She personally called on my behalf and filed the stop payment orders for a third time. This process took another 40 minutes, and I was again told it would take 10 business days for the claims to be processed and for my funds to be refunded. I was given the same claim numbers : XXXX XXXX As of today, XX/XX/XXXX, only one of the disputed charges has been refunded. When I called Wells Fargo for an update, I was told that a letter had been sent to mebut I never received any such letter. I asked why there was no record of this correspondence in my online banking messages, but the agent simply repeated that a letter had been mailed. 

Adding to my frustration, between the XX/XX/XXXX stop payment request and the XX/XX/XXXX re-submission, several additional unauthorized charges were deducted from my account. Oddly, one charge of {$190.00} from XXXX XXXX was refunded, but five others were notincluding more than {$1700.00} from XXXX. When I asked why some charges were refunded while others were not, the agent provided no clear answer and instead told me to " talk to the merchant. '' This entire experience has had a severe financial impact on my business. Because of these unauthorized withdrawals and Wells Fargo 's failure to act promptly, my business was unable to make critical payments, resulting in the termination of our company health insurance plan. The financial strain and uncertainty caused by the banks failure to execute basic stop payment requests have been immensely damaging. 

Beyond the monetary loss, the treatment I received from Wells Fargo 's customer service was appalling. With the exception of the in-branch banker, every phone representative I spoke with was dismissive, unhelpful, and outright rude. Instead of working to resolve the issue, they were defensive and seemed more concerned with shifting blame than assisting a long-time customer. At one point, an agent even suggested that the merchants might attempt to withdraw funds under different names, as if that somehow absolved the bank of responsibility. When I asked whether that wouldn't constitute fraud, I was met with silence and evasion.After 25+ years of banking with Wells Fargo , I am deeply disappointed by how this situation has been handled. The bank 's failure to act competently and in good faith has caused me financial and operational harm. I expect an immediate resolution and a full refund of my disputed funds.

Capitol One has failed to resolve the dispute within a reasonable time frame and I have reason to believe they are unfairly delaying my case. Here are the key details of my case : Transaction Date : XX/XX/scrub> 2024 Dispute Filed : XX/XX/scrub> 2024 Merchant : XXXX XXXX Amount Paid : {$220.00} Item Description : XXXX  Nature of Dispute : Goods never received Attempts to Resolve : I have contacted Capitol One multiple times via email, phone, and chat, yet they have failed to provide any resolution. Under Regulation E, debit card disputes, including those involving goods not received, must be resolved within 90 days or a provisional credit must be issued during the investigation. Capitol One has not issued a provisional credit and has not resolved the case within the required time frame. 

I request that Capitol One immediately : Issue a provisional credit for the amount of the disputed transaction. 
Complete the investigation and refund the amount of the transaction within the required timeframe. 
Confirm, in writing, that they have acknowledged their violation of Regulation E and will handle the dispute according to the regulations. 
I have been extremely patient, and Capitol Ones repeated delays and failure to properly classify this dispute are unacceptable.

FCRA 605B ( 15 U.S.C. 1681c-2 ) : If an account resulted from fraud or identity theft and you can not verify its legitimacy, the credit bureaus must block and remove it.

My credit report shows a reputed collection account XXXX with ONLINE INFORMATION SERVICE with different opening dates, balances, first date of delinquency, balance due, and/or last date of activities. I have never had an account with this company nor any record of any type of first notice of debt including rights to dispute from this company. And if I, by chance, even though I have no recollection nor tangible record, naively spoke with a representative of this company over the phone about this debt, I was not informed by that representative that I had a right to dispute this debt nor a specific timeframe to do so. 

15 USC 1692g 809. Validation of debts ( a ) Notice of debt ; contents states that within XXXX days after the initial communication with a consumer in connection with the collection of any debt, a debt collector shall, unless the following information is contained in the initial communication or the consumer has paid the debt, send the consumer a written notice containing ( XXXX ) a statement that unless the consumer, within XXXX days after receipt of the notice, disputes the validity of the debt, or any portion thereof, the debt will be assumed to be valid by the debt collector. XXXX XXXX XXXX definition of the word receipt is- a writing acknowledging the receiving of goods or money ; proof, evidence. I have never signed nor received any type of acknowledgement receipt from a mailing service for any mail from this company. I am familiar with the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ). Had I signed a receipt of notice for the proper and legal documentation from this company, I wouldve immediately responded asking for lawful verification of debt or copy of court ordered judgement well within the lawful 30 days allotted. After receiving my response letter with receipt, this company would have to legally cease from collection attempts and remove the account from my credit reports until their proof of verification is sent back to me. This company has reported to my credit reports without observing the FDCPA laws. My credit has been impacted adversely because of this companys irresponsibility. 

My credit reports also show that ONLINE INFORMATION SERVICE has provided this alleged account with inaccurate information. The FCRA requires that all data reported from the credit reporting agencies, creditors, or furnishers on a consumer 's report be 100 % ACCURATE, 100 % VERIFIABLE, and 100 % TIMELY. This means no data can be reported that can't be legally PROVEN to be 100 % accurate. 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( A ) ( 1 ) A person shall not furnish any information relating to a consumer to any consumer reporting agency if the person knows or has reasonable cause to believe that the information is inaccurate. My XXXX, XXXX, and XXXX credit reports all show different open dates, balances, first date of delinquency, balance due, and/or last date of activities for this same exact account. Therefore making this alleged account full of inaccuracies. 

This is erroneous and flawed reporting that is listed on my credit reports. Not only did ONLINE INFORMATION SERVICE not follow lawful FDCPA communications protocol, but it has also broken FDCPA False or Misleading Representations protocol as well. A debt collector, in collecting a debt, may not use any false, deceptive, or misleading representation. Specifically, a debt collector may not falsely represent the character, amount, or legal status of the debt, or of any services rendered, or compensation he or she may receive for collecting the debt. A debt collector may not communicate, or threaten to communicate, false credit information or information that should be known to be false, including not identifying disputed debts as such. Each of my 3 credit reports show different information instead of them all showing the exact same information. This is considered a false and misleading representation that this company has submitted to the credit reporting agencies. 

The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) has begun to aggressively litigate companies who continuously violate consumer laws. According to consumerfinance.gov, the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) took action against the nations XXXX largest debt buyers and collectors for using deceptive tactics to collect bad debts. The Bureau found that XXXX XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX XXXX bought debts that were potentially inaccurate, lacking documentation, or unenforceable. Without verifying the debt, the companies collected payments by pressuring consumers with false statements and churning out lawsuits using robo-signed court documents. The CFPB has ordered the companies to overhaul their debt collection and litigation practices and to stop reselling debts to third parties. 
The CFPB found that XXXX and XXXX XXXX XXXX attempted to collect debts that they knew, or should have known, were inaccurate or could not legally be enforced based on contractual disclaimers, past practices of debt sellers, or consumer disputes. The companies also filed lawsuits against consumers without having the intent to prove many of the debts, winning the vast majority of the lawsuits by default when consumers failed to defend themselves. These practices violated the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act and the XXXX XXXX XXXX Reform and Consumer Protection Act. 

The website also stated that Encore and XXXX XXXX XXXX threatened and deceived consumers to collect on debts they should have known were inaccurate or had other problems, said CFPB XXXX XXXX XXXX. Now, the XXXX biggest debt buyers in the market must refund millions and overhaul their practices. We will continue to take action to protect consumers from illegal and obnoxious debt collection practices. 

Just as the CFPB took action against the above companies, I am asking the CFPB to take action against this company as well. Please help me get this account removed immediately and conduct an investigation on this company. As a consumer, Im publicly publishing this descriptive complaint on consumerfinance.gov so that others can learn from my experience and so that this government agency can use this information to help work with other violations and complaints from consumers regarding this company. It is not my duty to provide evidence that this alleged debt is not mine. It is the legal obligation of the debt collector to first prove or provide proof of evidence that they can lawfully collect on any alleged debt before a consumer challenges it, accurately report to the credit agencies, and follow all FCRA and FDCPA laws. As of today, they have been very unsuccessful to do so.

Company Name : LoanDepot Product : Mortgage Sub-product : VA Mortgage Issue : Was denied credit Sub-issue : Was denied credit but not given a reason why Consumer Complaint Narrative : I applied for a VA cash-out refinance loan with LoanDepot ( Loan # XXXX ). During the loan process, I was initially told by the company that I could not qualify because I was not currently living in the home. 

As a veteran, I knew this was inaccurate. I provided them with the exact regulation from the VA Lenders Handbook, Chapter 3, Section 3, which states that the veteran only needs to intend to occupy the home within 60 days of closing not at the time of application. The text reads : " The veteran must certify that he or she intends to personally occupy the property as his or her home. The veteran need not occupy the property immediately, but must personally occupy the property as his or her home within a reasonable time after loan closing ( normally 60 days ). '' After I submitted this evidence, a LoanDepot representative ( XXXX XXXX ) told me that the issue was resolved. Then later, I was told again that occupancy was still a problem. Eventually, I was notified that my loan had been denied. 

I received an email saying that the reason for the denial could be found in their Secure Document Portal. However, after completing the identity verification steps, I was never able to access or view the specific reason for denial. This is a violation of the Equal Credit Opportunity Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1691 ( d ) ), which gives applicants the right to receive a statement of the principal reasons for adverse action.

I am requesting CFPB assistance in compelling LoanDepot to : Provide the specific underwriting or credit-related reason for the denial in writing ; Confirm whether the decision was based on the occupancy issue and, if so, provide the specific policy or rule they relied on ; Address any improper denial based on misinterpretation of VA occupancy guidelines. I have already filed a separate inquiry with the VA Regional Loan Center to investigate the matter from the VA side as well.

Desired Resolution : A full written explanation of the denial reason ( s ) Clarification of any policy used Review and correction of any improper handling of VA policy Potential reconsideration of my application if the denial was in error

Name : XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX  fl XXXX : To : Consumer adjustment co Date : XX/XX/year> In regards to : FDCPA Violations Account NumberXXXX Dear Compliance Department XXXX 
I ( XXXX XXXX ) a person, non-adverse, non-belligerent, non-combatant party and executer with full life. I have received a correspondence from you pertaining to an alleged debt you claim I owe. I want to make you aware that I am fully aware of my rights as a CONSUMER. An according to the FDCPA you have violated my federally protected rights. Your blatant negligence, willful noncompliance, harassment and abuse will not be tolerated. This letter also serves as a cease and desist. Please stop contacting me in regard to this alleged debt. Also please stop reporting it on my consumer credit report as you are in violation of the FDCPA. In accordance with the FDCPA you are in violation of both, 15 USC 1692 ( c ) Communication in connection with debt collection and 15 U.S. Code 1692b - Acquisition of location information.

My credit report shows a collection from your agency. I was never notified of this collection. Whats more, I do not believe this debt is accurate. Under the FAIR DEBT COLLECTION PRACTICES ACT, I have the right to request and receive validation of the debt. Therefore, please provide me with a copy of all the following : 1 ) An explanation of what this alleged account balance is for. 

2 ) A calculation of this balance, including the complete payment history on this account, so I have proof that the amount is correct.

3 ) Documentation that shows I agreed to pay this debt with my signature.

4 ) The Agreement that grants you authority to collect on this alleged debt.

5 ) A copy of your state license, including license number that give you rights to collect in my state. 15 USC 1692 ( c ) Communication in connection with debt collection ( a ) Communication with the consumer generally Without the prior consent of the consumer given directly to the debt collector or the express permission of a court of competent jurisdiction, a debt collector may not communicate with a consumer in connection with the collection of any debt. 
15 U.S. Code 1692b - Acquisition of location information.

Any debt collector communicating with any person other than the consumer for the purpose of acquiring location information about the consumer shall ( 1 ) identify himself, state that he is confirming or correcting location information concerning the consumer, and, only if expressly requested, identify his employer.

( 2 ) not state that such consumer owes any debt ; ( 4 ) not communicate by post card. 
( 5 ) not use any language or symbol on any envelope or in the contents of any communication effected by the mails or telegram that indicates that the debt collector is in the debt collection business or that the communication relates to the collection of a debt ; and.

Pursuant 15 U.S. Code 1681n - Civil liability for willful noncompliance ( a ) ( b ) ( c ) In general Any person who willfully fails to comply with any requirement imposed under this subchapter with respect to any consumer is liable to that consumer in an amount equal to the sum of ( 1 ) any actual damages sustained by the consumer as a result of the failure or damages of not less than {$100.00} and not more than {$1000.00} ; or in the case of liability of a natural person for obtaining a consumer report under false pretenses or knowingly without a permissible purpose, actual damages sustained by the consumer as a result of the failure or {$1000.00}, whichever is greater ; Also you have committed the following FDCPA Violations : 806. Harassment and abuse 807. False or misleading representations 808. Unfair practices 809. Validation of debts In accordance with the FDCPA you are liable for {$1000.00} per violation you committed in your communication with me the consumer. I am requesting a payment in the amount of {$5000.00} for the violations you have committed against me. Please make payment within 15 days of your receiving this notice. I will also be filing a formal complaint with the CFPB in regard to this matter. Please also be aware that if necessary I will move forward with further action against ( Company ), if you fail to comply with this notice. 
In accordance with the FDCPA please make check payable in the amount of XXXX and send to the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX fl XXXX

I am writing to formally dispute the collection account, reported by Williams and Fudge for the amount of {$1200.00}. This debt is being repeatedly reported and deleted from my credit report without the necessary proof of identification or validation of the debt. 

According to the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), I am entitled to request validation of this debt, and it is the responsibility of the creditor to prove that the debt belongs to me and that the collection is valid. Despite repeated attempts by the collection agency to report and delete the account, they have failed to provide adequate documentation to substantiate their claim. 

Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), I am also requesting that the credit bureau investigates the accuracy of the information reported. I ask that you provide evidence to support the collection agencys claim and that the account is mine, including : Proof of the original creditor and the amount owed. 

A copy of the signed agreement or contract establishing my responsibility for this debt. 

Any correspondence from the creditor or collection agency confirming the debt or showing proof of the alleged debt. 

In accordance with Section 809 of the FDCPA, I am requesting that you provide documentation to verify the debt within 30 days from the date of this letter. If this information is not provided within this time frame, the account should be marked as disputed, and any future reporting of this debt should be stopped. Under Section 1681i of the FCRA, I have the right to challenge the accuracy of information on my credit report, and failure to prove the debts validity should result in its removal.

Please consider this letter a formal request to investigate the account and provide proper validation or remove the collection from my credit report. I expect a written response within the legal time frame. If the requested validation is not provided, I will take further action, including filing complaints with the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) and seeking legal advice. 

Thank you for your attention to this matter. I look forward to your prompt response.

complaints.sub_issue: Problem using a debit or ATM card
complaints.consumer_complaint_narrative:
On XX/XX/XXXX, when I woke up from a nap around XXXX XXXX, I noticed several pending charges on my account that I had not made. I immediately called my bank ( Chime ). They said they can't do anything until the transactions post, and to call the merchant. So I do. The charges total almost {$600.00}. I called XXXX because at this point it's XXXX XXXX, and at that its the only merchant I can contact. I personally use XXXX and have the XXXX, which was clearly charged to my XXXX account a week or so ago. When I call XXXX, I give the last 4 numbers of my card, and sure enough! I didn't make these charges ; some lady named XXXX XXXX did. It is clearly shown that a second XXXX subscription has been bought with a card in the amount of {$9.00}. XXXX also says they can't do anything until the transaction posts. All of the charges are to a hotel in Ohio. I live in Florida. And my account clearly shows I have not been traveling anywhere. Who goes on vacation from Florida to Ohio anyway? 

The next morning, I called XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, which is in ... guess where? You guessed it. OHIO. The girl is very sympathetic. I give her the last four digits of my card. I hear her in the background, " Oh, I know who this is. '' However, she puts me on hold, speaks to her boss, and comes back to say that they can not release any further information.

Finally, when the transactions post, I am able to dispute them with my bank. When I call, they say she used a card that was reported lost a few years back. This is on the XXXX. This morning ( XX/XX/XXXX ), the investigation concluded that they will not be returning my money. I have filed a rebuttal and requested information on why the first investigation was closed in the first place. I have not received them yet. I have banked with Chime for over ten years, and I have probably had only one dispute in that whole time. I did not make these charges ; I should not be held liable for them. I reported them in an extremely timely fashion. I did not do anything wrong. My money is FDIC-insured and should be returned to me immediately.

There is no way that two simple phone calls proved to me that it wasn't me, but their " investigator '' didn't come to the same conclusions.

complaints.consumer_complaint_narrative:
On XX/XX/year>, I called Truist bank to close a joint checking account that was in my name and my son XXXX 's name. It was set up originally to make direct student loan payments to get the lowest rate, but once the loan was paid, funds were still left in the account ( {$950.00} ). I asked them to close the account and mail the check for the funds to my home address at XXXX XXXX XXXX in XXXX, MA. After XXXX weeks, I checked online to look for the account status, but I could no longer even access the account to see past history showing the last balance. I called back to find out status, and they confirmed the closing balance, then checked and indicated that a check was issued 7-10 days after I called, but that it was apparently sent to XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, MA, which had been my son 's college address more than 5 years ago. 

I asked if they could cancel and reissue the check to send to our home address. First the online account service on the weekend indicated they couldn't authorize, and that I needed to call back on Monday. On Monday, the online account service manager indicated that they did not have authority and that I needed to call a branch office. I called the closest branch office in NJ, and they indicated that they could only cancel and reissue the check if I came to the branch in person to sign forms. I asked if they could send forms that I could sign, notarize, and send back registered, and they said no, they had no other alternative but to come in person. complaints.consumer_complaint_narrative:
On XX/XX/2025, I used my FNBO debit card ( ending in XXXX ) to send a {$100.00} payment through XXXX  ( Transaction ID : [ insert if available ] ) to a freelancer for a custom video editing service for my company. The agreement was that the work would be delivered within XXXX to XXXX hours. I have full documentation of this agreement, including XXXX conversations and screenshots confirming delivery timelines and scope of work. 

Between XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX, I followed up repeatedly as the freelancer kept promising the video was nearly done but failed to deliver any work. These delays continued over two full weeks. I gave him numerous chances, but by XX/XX/XXXX, it was clear the service was not going to be provided. I never received a video or any usable deliverable despite multiple attempts to resolve it directly. 

On XX/XX/2025, I filed a formal dispute with FNBO requesting a chargeback under Regulation E. I clearly stated that this was a debit card transaction for services that were never delivered. However, FNBO denied the dispute on XX/XX/XXXX, stating that because the payment went through XXXX, it falls under money transfer rules and is outside their responsibility. They said XXXX only role is to transfer money, not ensure service delivery. 

This explanation is completely false under federal law. Regulation E, under 12 CFR 1005.11, requires FNBO to investigate and resolve errors for any electronic fund transfer made via debit card including cases where the customer did not receive what they paid for. The method of payment ( debit card ), not the merchant type, triggers Regulation E protection. 

XXXX is simply a payment processor, not the actual recipient of the funds. The end recipient was the service provider who failed to fulfill the paid agreement. FNBOs denial ignores the core purpose of Regulation E which is to protect consumers in situations exactly like this. 

At no point did FNBO conduct a meaningful investigation. They did not request documentation from me ( which I offered ) nor inquire about the nature of the transaction. Their dismissal appears to be based on internal policy not federal compliance. 

I am asking the CFPB to hold FNBO accountable to its obligations under Regulation E. I am requesting : That FNBO be required to reopen this dispute.

That they conduct a proper investigation based on the non-receipt of services.

That they issue a refund of {$100.00} in accordance with Regulation E. 

I have copies of all relevant evidence, including : WhatsApp messages showing agreed timelines and non-delivery Screenshots of repeated delays and unfulfilled promises The XXXX  payment receipt ( At no point did I select Friends and Family or make a personal transfer this was a debit card-funded payment for business services under a professional agreement. There is no basis for treating this as a personal remittance or exempting it from consumer protections. ) FNBOs denial letter FNBO is trying to avoid responsibility by hiding behind the money transfer label but XXXX is simply the vehicle. The transaction remains a debit card-funded electronic payment for services, which falls squarely under Regulation E protections. 

Thank you for your help in enforcing these federal protections and ensuring the bank does not avoid responsibility for rightful dispute resolution.

I believe this conduct may constitute deceptive or unfair acts or practices ( UDAAP ) under consumer protection laws.

Before anything else happens with this account, I need Jefferson Capital to show that it actually has the legal right to collect it. If you believe this debt belongs to me, then the documentation should exist to support that claim. 

Start by explaining how Jefferson Capital became involved with this account. If the account originated with another creditor and was later sold, provide documentation showing the chain of ownership from the original creditor through every company that possessed the account before it reached your organization. I want to see the assignments and any bill of sale or transfer agreement that specifically identifies this account. 

I am also requesting the original records that created the alleged debt. That means the agreement that supposedly opened the account, the terms and conditions that applied at that time, and any updated versions that may have been issued later. In addition, provide the account statements and transaction history from the original creditor that show the activity you claim occurred. Internal summaries or collection notes are not sufficient. I am requesting the original account-level documentation created by the original creditor. 

If the amount currently being reported is greater than the balance at charge-off, explain how that number was calculated. Identify the contractual provision that allowed those charges and the legal authority permitting them. 

Jefferson Capital should also identify the individual within the company who has direct knowledge of the account records being relied upon. I am not asking for someone who simply reviewed a database entry. I am asking for the person who can confirm the authenticity of the records and establish a prima facie case consistent with XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX, XXXX [ XXXX ]. That person must also be familiar with the original creditors record-keeping practices as described in XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ]. 

Please also provide the date of the last payment made to the original creditor. If this account is outside the statute of limitations, you may not misrepresent its legal enforceability under 15 U.S.C. 1692e ( 5 ). complaints.consumer_complaint_narrative: I attempted to contact the firm via their form on XX/XX/XXXX, I called and spoke to someone on XX/XX/XXXX who gave me information and then escalated to her supervisor XXXX, who provided additional information, which contradicted the first person. I had been told by my contractor verbally and in writing that the loan would be 0 % interest for 12 months. I asked multiple times via email for clarification on the language in the contract, which was validated as correct. I would've paid in full the cash amount, but it made more financial sense to take the loan for 12 months, and then pay it off when interest began to accrue afterwards. When I called to get my payoff amount, it was $ XXXX higher than I anticipated based on the starting balance, and the 14 payments I had made. When I spoke with XXXX he explained that because I didn't pay off the loan DURING the promotional period, the promotion was retroactively rescinded and the full balance had accumulated 17.99 % interest the entire time. So it wasn't a 0 % interest, it was a deferral, that was then retroactively applied in full after the 12 month promotional period. This is highly confusing, different than what was communicated, and misleading. I requested they immediately cease pulling via ACH from my account ( I paid the monthly payment automatically in full on time each month ). The balance at the end of the 12 month period was {$9600.00} ( per XXXX ), and then because I didn't pay that balance in full prior to that day, even though all payments were made on time and continued to be paid, my balance jumped $ XXXX. The company only makes money if consumers DON'T adhere to the promotional period- so the company, Service Finance, is incentivized to have consumers miss out on the promotional period in order to recoup any gains from lending. This is especially harmful to lower income individuals who rely on these programs to help repair their homes. Loan was created in XX/XX/XXXX for XXXX Monthly payments were made via ACH ( auto, on time ) for {XXXX Promotion as described verbally/writing by contractor was 0 % interest for 12 months, and 18 % afterwards I paid all monthly amounts on time, and called XX/XX/XXXX to payoff the balance I was told the balance was still {XXXX which surprised me because it was ~ $ XXXX more than I expected. Further investigation uncovered it was a deferred interest loan that retroactively applied in full if the entire loan wasn't paid within 12 months, which negates the value of a promotional period for all individuals who can't pay the loan in full in a short window. This also contradicts my understanding of the loan. A promotional period implies a value to the consumer - not a term that triggers a retroactive fee application- which is confusing, misleading, and harmful to consumers who are trying to navigate complex financial documents and understand financing terms.

complaints.consumer_complaint_narrative:
I am the author of this complaint. 


According to the Fair Credit Reporting Act 15 USC 1681 section 602a states " there is a need to ensure that consumer reporting agencies exercise their grave responsibilities with fairness, impartiality, and a respect for the consumers right to privacy. " XXXX, XXXX and Experian are consumer reporting agencies and I am the consumer. 


I have the right to make sure my private information isn't shared which is backed by 15 USC 6801 which states " It is the policy of the Congress that each financial institution has an affirmative and continuing obligation to respect the privacy of its customers and to protect the security and confidentiality of those customers nonpublic personal information. '' XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX, and XXXX XXXX XXXX is a financial institution by definition under that title. 15 USC 1681 section 604 a section 2 states that " In general Subject to subsection ( c ), any consumer reporting agency may furnish a consumer report under the following circumstances and no other : in accordance with the written instructions of the consumer to whom it relates. '' XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX and the consumer reporting agencies XXXX, XXXX, and Experian do not have my consent to furnish this information and they surely do not have my written consent. Any and all consent to XXXX, XXXX, Experian, to furnish anything in regard to these accounts, whether it be verbal, non-verbal, written, implied or otherwise, is revoked. 15 USC 6802 ( b ) ( c ) states that " A financial institution may not disclose nonpublic personal information to a nonaffiliated third party unless the consumer is given an explanation of how the consumer can exercise that nondisclosure option. '' XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX, and XXXX XXXX XXXX never informed me of my right to exercise my nondisclosure option. Not only that, 15 USC 1681C ( a ) ( 5 ) states " except as authorized under subsection ( b ), no consumer reporting agency may also make any consumer report containing any of the following items of information Any other adverse item of information, other than records of convictions of crimes which antedates the report by more than seven years. '' These accounts are adverse items, and they are reporting without my permission, which is against the law. 15 U.S. Code 1681s2 ( A ) ( 1 ) A states " A person shall not furnish any information relating to a consumer to any consumer reporting agency if the person knows or has reasonable cause to believe that the information is inaccurate. 15 U.S. Code 1681e states every consumer reporting agency shall maintain reasonable procedures designed to avoid violations of section 1681c of this title and to limit the furnishing of consumer reports to the purposes listed under section 1681b of this title. XXXX, XXXX and Experian are not maintaining reasonable procedures. Also 12 CFR 1016.7 states that " a consumer may exercise the right to opt out at any time. '' I am opting out of your reporting services in regard to these accounts.
